hunters.text: What ships, and the accepted design

The hunter's freeze and the controller's deposit rotation, which unfreezes, are one transaction each in this generation of the checkpoint program; ckeri freeze submits the freeze and ckeri advance --deposit the deposit rotation. The top-up transaction runs through the production scripts on a local test chain; ckeri top-up plans for preprod only and needs a manifest with a premium, which no committed manifest has until the redeployment (#356). These run on a local test chain and are not deployed to preprod; this code is not for mainnet. Play The pool runs dry, so Hal freezes her instead and Two hunters race.

Hal is a hunter: anyone paid to land an owner's rotation on chain, or to freeze a checkpoint whose pool cannot pay for one. He watches Alice's witnesses. When they receipt a rotation, he lands it and the chain pays him the premium P (the fee for landing a rotation) from her pool of advance funds. That is story 2 on the checkpoint simulation. In KERI's vocabulary Hal is a watcher with a wage; the receipts he waits for are the ones KERI's witnessing policy requires.

When the pool cannot cover P, he freezes her instead. He presents the later rotation as evidence, exactly as the log exports it, and takes the freeze bond B (what a hunter takes when the pool cannot pay). The datum keeps its old keys and sequence number; only the frozen flag is set, and the checkpoint then holds the minimum ADA, the deposit and the pool. ckeri freeze --aid … --kel rotation.cesr … lands it and pays the bond to the funding address. The checkpoint is inert to everyone but the next keys: consumers reject it; a second freeze is refused; the poison (the owner's own lock on the checkpoint) still belongs to the current quorum.

Alice unfreezes with her next witnessed rotation, landed with the deposit option: ckeri advance --deposit … writes the exact bytes her new keys sign, an intent that names the network, the checkpoint policy, the spent output, her identifier, the new sequence number, the new epoch and the amount, and lands the rotation with those signatures. The successor is unfrozen and holds B again, so the checkpoint is consumable again; the premium is paid exactly when the pool covers it, as for any rotation. Nobody else can choose the deposit option for her rotation, and a signature for one output is worthless for another. On a checkpoint that is not frozen the intent names an amount of zero and the deposit brings nothing. See Rotate your preprod identity for the commands and The deposit intent for what is signed.

Anyone may top up the pool by at least one premium, once between two rotations; nobody signs anything. The top-up sets a mark in the datum and changes nothing else. Every rotation clears the mark and a freeze keeps it. A freeze is refused while the pool covers the premium. ckeri top-up, with the identifier and the amount, builds and submits the top-up; it plans for preprod only and needs a manifest with a premium, which no committed manifest has until the redeployment (#356). It refuses an amount below the premium and a checkpoint already topped up since its last rotation before it builds anything.

Two hunters can race the same rotation. One winner, one refusal. The closer chooses when the reap (the owner's close, a rotation by the next keys) happens, never who is paid: a copied reap with the payee rewritten is refused.

The earlier freeze-for-lag, ACTIVE to ARMED with a deadline and a claim, is gone: nothing arms, waits or claims. The freeze that remains is what a hunter takes when the owner's pool has run dry, in a single transaction.
See Rotate, Poison, and the consumer checklist.
